Verily it is the one who hates you who is cut off [from all
goodness].
Here Allah (4g) says to His Prophet Muhammad (Jig), reminding
him of His favours to him: ^Verily We have granted you [O Muhammad]
abundance [al-kawthar]$ that is, much goodness and great favours,
among which is what Allah will grant to His Prophet (^) on the Day
of Resurrection of the river which is called al-Kawthar.
He will also grant him the Cistern ( al-hawd ), the length of which
is a month’s journey, as is its width; its water is whiter than milk
and sweeter than honey, and its vessels are like the stars of the sky
Juz ' 30
in their number and brightness. Whoever takes one sip from it will
never ever thirst again.
Having mentioned His favours to him, He commands him to give
thanks for them, as He says:
{■(so pray to your Lord and offer your sacrifice to Him alonep these two
acts of worship are singled out for mention, because they are among
the best and greatest acts of worship that bring one closer to Allah.
In prayer one feels humility before Allah and shows it physically, for
prayer demonstrates submission and servitude to Him.
In the case of sacrifice, one draws closer to Allah with the best
quality of sacrificial animals that one possesses, giving wealth that
one has a natural inclination to love and want to keep to oneself.
{•(Verily it is the one who hates you’p that is, the one who despises
you, criticises you and shows disrespect towards you
(•(who is cut off [from all goodnessjb for his deeds will cease and no
one will remember him.
As for Muhammad he is the one who is perfect in the true
sense of the word, who is to attain all that is possible of perfection in
the case of a created being, such as high renown and large number
of supporters and followers.
I’ll is is the end of the commentary on Soorat al-Kawthar.
All praise and thanks are lor Allah, and may the blessings and
peace of Allah he upon Prophet Muhammad (^*). his family, and
his Companions abundantly until the Day of Judgement.
Soorat al-Kafiroon
In the name of Allah,
the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful
